prerequisites: Basic knowledge of measurement technology and information processing
Basic knowledge of operational processes and organizational structures in companies

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have knowledge of common conveying and storage equipment up to handling technology.
Students will differentiate the used technologies regarding their efficiency and sustainability.
Students will be able to delimit and illustrate corresponding system technology.
Students will be able to explain and classify their methodical knowledge for the analysis and planning of material flows.
Students will be able to explain the functionalities and specifics of supply chains.
Students will be able to estimate and compare the application possibilities of common material flow technologies.
Students will be able to justify the choice of loading aids and transport vehicles and compare the use of feeding techniques.
Students will be able to present throughput considerations in storage systems and order picking strategies.
Students will know necessary material flow data for optimization purposes and justify the design of transport networks with this knowledge.
Students will have knowledge of planning and simulation in a holistic material flow consideration.
Students will be able to plan material flow systems and simulate them using appropriate software.
Students will be able to apply methods for the selection of conveying and storage equipment and to design, shape, and implement corresponding system technology.
Students will be able to perform capacity and throughput calculations in the analysis and planning of material flow systems and transfer the results to new or adaptation plans.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals: Material flow and logistics in the corporate environment, definitions within logistical systems
Unit loads: Packaging, loading aids, formation of loading units
Conveying technology: Continuous conveyors, intermittent conveyors, transport vehicles, handling and feeding technology
Storage technology: System technology, capacity planning, stacker cranes, throughput considerations
Order picking technology: Strategies, technical design, information flows
Information and control technology: Data/data analysis for optimization purposes, object localization, transport route design, route planning
Holistic material flow considerations: Supply chains: functionalities, organization, reliability, efficiency, sustainability
Planning and simulation: Planning methods, system design, simulation strategies, processing of simulation tasks
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is determined by the lecturer: Oral examination or portfolio examination. The portfolio examination consists of four elements: 3 semester-long written project reports (max 20 points each) and 1 term paper (max 40 points), for a total of 100 points. The experimental work is an ungraded examination performance, consisting of approximately 4 to 5 experimental tasks.
